problems.title: Cycle of the units digit
problems.question: Find the last digit of 2017¹⁹⁹.
problems.idea: Only the final digit of the base matters.
steps: Use the third digit in the cycle: 3.

problems.title: Divide two equal nonzero products
problems.question: a⁴-b⁴=80 and (a²+b²)(a+b)=80. Find a-b.
problems.idea: Factor the first expression and compare.
steps: The product (a+b)(a²+b²) is 80, so it is nonzero.
The first equation becomes 80(a-b)=80, giving a-b=1.

problems.title: Match coefficients in a polynomial identity
problems.question: x²+x+m=(x+n)² for every x. Find m+n.
problems.idea: Expand the square and match coefficients.
steps: The x coefficient gives 2n=1, so n=1/2.
The constant gives m=n²=1/4. Thus m+n=3/4.

problems.title: Keep both square roots
problems.question: Solve 25x²-4=0 by factoring.
problems.idea: Use a difference of squares.
problems.note: Both roots are required. A choice listing only one is not the full solution set.

problems.title: Do not lose a zero root
problems.question: Solve 4y²-8y=0 by factoring.
problems.idea: Extract the common factor before dividing.
steps: A product vanishes if either factor does.

problems.title: Difference of two squared linear expressions
problems.question: Factor 49(x-y)²-36(x+y)².
problems.idea: Use the difference-of-squares identity.
steps: Multiply them to obtain the factorization.

problems.title: Multiply powers of monomials
problems.question: Simplify (-2x²y²/3)⁴·((9/4)xy³)³.
problems.idea: Raise coefficients and multiply exponents within each factor.
steps: The coefficient is (16/81)(729/64)=9/4; the even fourth power makes it positive.
The x exponent is 8+3=11 and y exponent 8+9=17.

problems.title: Minimum by completing the square
problems.question: Find the minimum of 9x²-12x+3.
problems.idea: Write the expression as a square plus a constant.
steps: The square is at least zero.
It is zero at x=2/3, so the lower bound -1 is attained.

problems.title: A telescoping polynomial product
problems.question: Simplify (1-x)(1+x+x²+…+x¹⁰).
problems.idea: Subtract the shifted sum.
steps: Multiplying by 1 leaves the original sum, while multiplying by -x gives its negative shifted one place.

problems.title: Group a numerical expression
problems.question: Evaluate 77.3·13+8·37.3-77.3·8-13·37.3.
problems.idea: Factor the two repeated differences.

problems.title: Extract two common factors
problems.question: Find a²b-ab+a²c-ac if a=4 and b+c=5.
problems.idea: Group by b and c.

problems.title: Greatest altitude to a fixed hypotenuse
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse 16 cm. Find the greatest possible altitude to it.
problems.idea: The product of its legs is largest when they are equal.
steps: Equality holds for equal legs, so the bound is attainable.

problems.title: Successive projections in a right triangle
problems.question: C=90°,A=30°,AC=10 cm. CD⊥AB and DE⊥AC. Find AE.
problems.idea: Project first onto AB, then back onto AC.

problems.title: The obtuse apex identifies the equal sides
problems.question: ABC is isosceles and its exterior angle at C is 88°. Which sides are equal?
problems.idea: The interior angle at C is obtuse.
formulas: Interior+adjacent exterior=180°; a triangle cannot have two obtuse angles.
steps: C=92°, so C cannot be one of two equal base angles.
It must be the apex, making the incident sides CA,CB equal.

problems.title: Three triangle inequalities with integer sides
problems.question: Triangles have sides (1,4,a),(2,3,b),(a,b,x), all a,b,x positive integers. Maximize x.
problems.idea: Bound a and b separately first.
steps: Choose a=b=4,x=7; all three triangles are nondegenerate.

problems.title: Exterior angles sum to a full turn
problems.question: Triangle exterior angles have ratio 3:4:5. Find the least interior angle.
problems.idea: Use one exterior angle at each vertex.

problems.title: Equal distances locate an internal point
problems.question: In ABC, D∈AB with DB=2AD, K∈DC, AK=KC, ACD=15°,BAC=45°. Find KBC.
problems.idea: Normalize AD=1 and use the forced ray angles.
formulas: Equal sides have equal opposite angles; coordinate slope tanθ; dot-product angle rule.
steps: Choose A=(0,0),D=(1,0),B=(3,0). Since AC makes 45° with AB and DC makes 60°, their intersection is C=((3+√3)/2,(3+√3)/2).
AK=KC gives K on the perpendicular bisector of AC, namely Kx+Ky=(3+√3)/2. Intersecting this with DC gives K=(3/2,√3/2).
The ray BK makes 150° with the positive x-axis and BC makes 105°, so KBC=150°-105°=45°.

problems.title: An obtuse solution is also possible
problems.question: The altitudes of ABC meet at H and AB=CH. Find angle C.
problems.idea: Use the circumradius identities with an absolute value.
steps: Squaring gives sin²C=cos²C, yielding C=45° or 135°.
Both acute and obtuse triangles can realize the condition.
problems.answer: 45° or 135°; the printed choices include only 45°.
problems.note: The question does not say the triangle is acute. Dropping the absolute value in the orthocentre distance would lose the 135° solution.

problems.title: Total degree of a polynomial product
problems.question: Find positive integer n if (2xⁿ⁺¹y³-3x³y²+y⁴+1)(x²y²+(2/3)xⁿy³) has total degree 15.
problems.idea: For large enough n the highest-degree monomials are unique and cannot cancel.
formulas: Total degree of xᵖyᑫ is p+q; nonzero polynomial product degrees add.
steps: For n≥2 the first factor has degree n+4 and second n+3, so the product degree is 2n+7.
For n=1 the factor degrees are 5 and 4, giving only 9, so no smaller case was missed.

problems.title: A bisector ratio fixes a right triangle shape
problems.question: C=90°, BD bisects B, AD=2DC and BD=4. Find AC.
problems.idea: Apply the angle-bisector theorem.
formulas: AD/DC=AB/BC; a right triangle with hypotenuse twice a leg is 30–60–90.
steps: In right triangle BCD, angle CBD=30°, so DC=BD/2=2.

problems.title: Cancel variable terms in a square expression
problems.question: Simplify (2a+5)²-(2a+5)(2a-5)+(2a-5)²-4a²-25.
problems.idea: Set u=2a,v=5 and expand symmetrically.

problems.title: Two possible signs of a sum
problems.question: a²+b²=31, ab=9. Find possible a+b.
problems.idea: Square the sum.
steps: Thus a+b=±7. Both are attainable; the corresponding quadratic with product 9 has discriminant 49-36=13>0.
problems.answer: a+b=7 or -7. The listed positive option is 7.

problems.title: A perpendicular ray and an isosceles triangle
problems.question: In the diagram F,X,U,Y are collinear, XZ=YZ, XU=UY, EXZ=90°,XZY=130°. Find FXE.
problems.idea: The base angles of XYZ are equal.
steps: EXZ=90° and F lies opposite Y from X as drawn.

problems.title: Quadratic terms cancel in a rational equation
problems.question: Solve (2x-1)(x+3)/3-(4x-1)(x-1)/6=1.
problems.idea: Clear denominators and expand carefully.

problems.title: Use the 45-degree corner of an isosceles right triangle
problems.question: The diagram gives AC=BC,ACB=90°,DAC=90°,DEA=55°, with A,B,E collinear and F on the extension of DA. Find FDE.
problems.idea: Transfer the 45° base angle into triangle ADE.
formulas: Isosceles right-triangle base angles=45°; exterior angle is supplementary.
steps: CAB=45°. With DA⊥AC and AE on the AB ray, DAE=90°-45°=45°.
